newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia loan recovery improving - central bank.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia loan recovery improving - central bank.

text.p: There has been an improvement in the recovery of Indonesian bank loans, the Central Bank Governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said.
He told a parliamentary hearing on Wednesday that overall credit recovery until August this year had improved although there were some "fluctuations" from time to time. He did not elaborate.
A copy of Djiwandono's written reply to the hearing was made available to Reuters on Thursday.
Figures in his presentation showed that non-performing loans in August totalled 10.43 percent or 31.69 trillion rupiah of the total outstanding loans of 303.75 trillion rupiah.
This compared with 10.42 percent or 27.89 trillion rupiah in December 1995 on outstanding loans of 267.81 trillion rupiah.
Non-performing loans stood at 11.62 percent or 27.87 trillion rupiah in December 1994 on oustanding loans of 239.73 trillion rupiah.
Bad debts amounted to 3.4 percent or 10.34 trillion rupiah of total oustanding loans in August, compared with 3.29 percent in December 1995 and 4.16 percent in December 1994.
Performing loans declined marginally to 89.57 percent or 272.06 trillion rupiah in August from 89.59 percent in December 1995 but rose against the 88.37 percent in December 1994.
